content:
jen: Heads-up — I'm running a small sim comparing FIFO, strict-priority, and a hybrid per-route token-bucket + slotting scheme on the eu-west GPU pool. Saw head-of-line blocking with FIFO starting ~85% saturation. Thoughts on fairness vs throughput tradeoffs?

omar: Nice. Can you paste the sim config? curious about arrival distribution + seq len mix.

jen: short config paste:```
adm_mode: hybrid
per_route_buckets: true
slot_count: 6
token_rate: 50tokens/s
bucket_capacity: 200
priority_aging_s: 20
```

ravi: Two quick notes: 1) token bucket helps isolate noisy tenants, 2) slotting avoids tiny-requests hogging headrooms. But slot_count interacts badly with long ctx lengths.

liz: +1. Also watch starvation when strict priorities exist. priority_aging helps but pick window carefully. We burned cpu cycles tuning aging to avoid oscillation. :grimacing: 

kai: Did you try allowing preemptible slots for short low-cost requests? like reserve 1 slot for <64 tokens requests, fallback to cheaper model if no slot free. reduced p99 a lot for small chats.

jen: I did a variant: reserve 1 small-slot + fallback to small-model. p99 for small reqs dropped from 2.2s -> 0.6s. overall GPU utilization went up ~4%. cost: small-model served ~12% of tokens but cut latency hotspots.

omar: How are you estimating request cost? simple tokens or sequence-length*kv-overhead?

jen: we used predicted token count from header + avg decode rate, and an empirical multiplier for kv/cache effect by model type. crude but good enough for admission.

ravi: We should also think about cross-region capacity. If eu-west is saturated we route to eu-central with slightly higher egress cost but lower queueing. Smart routing + admission = big win.

liz: Agree. Also track fairness metrics (Jain index) and tail error rates when you enable preemption. We saw preemption causing retries and extra tokens.

kai: Ops ask: what SLOs are we optimizing? p95 latency, p99 latency, or completed throughput per-dollar?

jen: For sim I optimized for p99 small-req latency and overall requests/sec. We can run multi-objective later.

omar: Could we try a token-bucket per-tenant + shared global queue for excess with priority aging? That keeps isolation but allows burst absorption.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: note: canary admission config pushed to staging: adm_mode=hybrid, per_route_buckets=true, slot_count=6. Monitor: /dash/queueing/canary-eu-west.

liz: When testing, add these metrics: queue_length_by_route, drop_rate_by_tenant, avg_slots_held, preempt_count, model_fallback_rate, gpu_util_percent. Also export the admission decisions for 1% sampled requests to debug.

jen: will run another sim with per-tenant buckets + global overflow + preemptible small slots. sharing results here in ~2h. thanks all. :heart:

omar: If you want help setting up the fairness dashboard ping me, I have a jupyter that computes Jain and starvation heatmaps.

jen: pinged you. attaching sim script next message.

jen: ```python
# tiny sim snippet (pseudo)
while t < horizon:
  req = sample_request()
  cost = estimate_cost(req)
  if tenant_bucket[req.tenant].tokens >= cost and free_slot():
    admit(req)
  else:
    overflow_queue.push(req)
  refill_buckets(dt)
  age_priorities(dt)
```

ravi: Perfect. Keep an eye on network egress when rerouting cross-region. costs + latency spike on inter-region deps (DBs) can break assumptions.

jen: noted. will cap cross-region fallbacks to 10% of overflow in sim.

ops-bot: metrics-bot: canary check: p99_small=0.62s, p99_all=1.9s, gpu_util=82% (1h window). No alerts.

jen: great, thanks. I'll post full sim CSV and graphs after run completes.
